stories.headline: China Blocks Meta's $2B Acquisition of AI Startup Manus, Orders Deal Unwound

key_facts.fact: China's NDRC ordered Meta to unwind its $2 billion-plus acquisition of agentic AI startup Manus, citing violations of export controls and national security regulations.

Manus became a sensation in early 2025 after releasing what it called the world's first 'general AI agent'; its core technology was developed by teams in Beijing and Wuhan before the company moved operations to Singapore.
Manus co-founders were summoned to meetings with Chinese officials in March and have since been barred from leaving the country.
Beijing feared the move was a blueprint for 'technology leakage,' where homegrown Chinese AI innovation is quietly moved abroad to be acquired by American companies.
The block coincides with the White House issuing directives accusing China of running 'industrial-scale' efforts to steal US AI technology.

stories.headline: Intellia Reports Positive Phase 3 CRISPR Results: 87% Attack Reduction, Files for FDA Approval

key_facts.fact: Lonvo-z reduced HAE attacks by 87% versus placebo in the Phase 3 HAELO trial, with a mean monthly attack rate of 0.26 vs 2.10 (p<0.0001)
62% of patients in the lonvo-z arm were entirely attack-free and therapy-free for the six-month evaluation period, versus 11% in placebo (p<0.0001)
This is the first Phase 3 readout for any in vivo CRISPR gene editing therapy worldwide
Intellia initiated a rolling BLA submission to the FDA and anticipates U.S. launch in the first half of 2027 if approved
80 patients were enrolled: 52 received lonvo-z and 28 placebo; all TEAEs were mild or moderate with no serious adverse events in the lonvo-z arm

stories.headline: Iran's Araghchi Meets Putin in St. Petersburg as US Ceasefire Talks Hit Impasse

key_facts.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in St. Petersburg on Monday to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss ceasefire diplomacy
The April 8 ceasefire mediated by Pakistan has been strained by disputes over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the US blockade on Iranian ports
Trump scrapped plans to send envoy Witkoff and Kushner to Islamabad for talks with Iran, citing 'tremendous infighting and confusion' within Tehran's leadership
Iranian President Pezeshkian reiterated that Tehran will not enter negotiations while the US blockade remains in place
Araghchi visited Oman and twice visited Pakistan over the weekend before heading to Russia, building multi-channel diplomatic outreach

stories.headline: Iran War Disrupts PCB Supply Chain; Goldman Says Prices Surged Up to 40% in April

key_facts.fact: The Middle East conflict disrupted supplies of crucial raw materials for printed circuit boards, pushing up prices for tech firms globally
Goldman Sachs reports PCB prices surged as much as 40% month-over-month in April
Only five ships including one Iranian oil tanker passed through the Strait of Hormuz in a 24-hour period on Friday, according to shipping data
Brent crude stayed above $107 amid the tensions; Citi raised its 2026 Brent forecast to $150 citing the Hormuz deadlock
Oil prices jumped more than 2% on Monday as US-Iran peace talks stalled and Hormuz shipments remained limited

stories.headline: Iran War Disrupts PCB Supply Chain: Goldman Sachs Reports 40% Price Surge After SABIC Plant Strike

key_facts.fact: PCB prices surged as much as 40% month-over-month in April, according to Goldman Sachs analysts
Iranian forces struck Saudi Arabia's Jubail Industrial City petrochemical complex in early April, halting SABIC's production of PPE resin used in PCB laminates
SABIC accounts for approximately 70% of the world's supply of high-purity polyphenylene ether (PPE) resin, the critical base material for PCB laminates
A South Korean supplier to Samsung and AMD says epoxy resin wait times have stretched from three weeks to fifteen
PCBs are used in almost all electronic devices including AI servers that hyperscalers are racing to deploy

stories.headline: Meta Signs Deal With Overview Energy for 1GW of Space Solar Power for AI Data Centers

key_facts.fact: Meta signed a first-of-its-kind agreement with Overview Energy for up to 1GW of space solar energy capacity, with orbital demonstration in 2028 and commercial power delivery expected in 2030.

Overview's system collects solar energy via satellites in geosynchronous orbit and beams it as low-intensity near-infrared light to existing solar facilities on the ground, enabling around-the-clock power.
The beam is invisible, less intense than sunlight, and passively safe for humans, animals, and aircraft according to Overview.
Meta is one of the first major companies to secure rights for future space solar energy capacity; the deal is positioned as strengthening America's energy leadership.
Overview's advisory board includes former NASA Administrator Jim Bridenstine, former NASA Administrator Mike Griffin, and former FERC Chairman Joseph Kelliher.

stories.headline: China's Moore Threads Swings to Q1 Profit as Revenue Surges 155%, Secures $91M GPU Cluster Order

key_facts.fact: Moore Threads Q1 2026 revenue reached RMB 738 million (~$102M), up 155.35% year-over-year
Net profit attributable to shareholders turned positive at RMB 29 million (~$4M), up from a RMB 113 million loss a year earlier
Full-year 2025 revenue was RMB 1.505 billion (~$208M), up 243% YoY, with gross margin of 65.57%
In March 2026, Moore Threads secured a RMB 660 million (~$91M) order for its KUAE intelligent computing cluster
R&D spending reached RMB 1.305 billion in 2025 — equivalent to 86.68% of revenue — with 2,014 IP applications filed including 1,743 invention patents
The company is developing next-generation 100,000-GPU-scale clusters based on its new 'Huagang' architecture

stories.headline: Chinese GPU Maker Moore Threads Swings to Q1 Profit, Revenue Up 155% YoY to $107M

key_facts.fact: Moore Threads reported Q1 2026 revenue of RMB 738 million (~$107M), up 155.35% year-over-year, swinging to a net profit of RMB 29 million (~$4.3M) from a net loss of ~$16.5M a year earlier.
Full-year 2025 revenue reached RMB 1.505 billion, up 243.37% YoY, with a gross margin of 65.57%.
The company secured a RMB 660 million (~$96M) order for a KUAE intelligent computing cluster in March 2026.
R&D spending reached RMB 1.305 billion in 2025, equal to 86.68% of revenue, with 2,014 IP applications filed including 1,743 invention patents.
Shares surged on Monday following the results as the company advances its 100,000-GPU cluster development.

stories.headline: Musk vs Altman Trial Begins: Jury Selection Starts in Oakland Over OpenAI's Nonprofit Origins

key_facts.fact: Jury selection began Monday in Oakland federal court for Elon Musk's civil trial against Sam Altman and others over OpenAI's transformation from a nonprofit, expected to last several weeks.
U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers dismissed Musk's fraud claims at his request but allowed breach-of-charitable-trust and unjust-enrichment claims to proceed.
Musk has sought damages of approximately $150 billion according to Reuters, with The Guardian citing a $134 billion estimate.
Unsealed court filings include private emails, texts, and diary entries from Musk, Altman, and other Silicon Valley participants.
The lawsuit alleges OpenAI's shift from nonprofit to for-profit violated founding commitments; Microsoft is named as a major investor.

stories.headline: OpenAI Publishes Five-Principle Framework for AGI, Altman Concedes Company's Larger Scale

key_facts.fact: OpenAI published a five-principle framework for AGI development on Sunday: democratization, empowerment, universal prosperity, resilience, and adaptability.
Altman concedes OpenAI is 'materially larger' than at the time of the 2018 Charter and acknowledges scenarios where the company 'may have to trade off some empowerment for more resilience.'
The framework is OpenAI's most prominent statement of intent since the 2018 Charter and arrives as US and European regulators tighten oversight of frontier AI labs.
Altman writes 'We deserve an enormous amount of scrutiny given the weight of what we are doing' and commits to resisting AI technology that consolidates power 'in the hands of the few.'
The post revisits OpenAI's 2019 decision to delay GPT-2 weights, calling the worry 'misplaced' but crediting it with discovering the iterative deployment strategy the company uses today.

stories.headline: Kuo: OpenAI Working With MediaTek and Qualcomm on AI Smartphone Chips for 2028 Launch

key_facts.fact: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reports OpenAI is working with MediaTek and Qualcomm to develop smartphone processors for an AI-focused phone, with mass production expected in 2028.
Key processor design considerations include power consumption, memory hierarchy management, and basic small-model execution, with complex tasks handled by cloud AI.
Chip specs and suppliers are expected to be finalized in late 2026 or Q1 2027.
Chinese supplier Luxshare will be the exclusive system co-design and manufacturing partner for the phone.
The phone would need to 'continuously' understand user context, suggesting extensive always-on AI functionality.

stories.headline: German AI Robotics Startup Sereact Raises $110M Series B Led by Headline

key_facts.fact: Sereact raised $110 million in a Series B round led by Headline, with new investors including Bullhound Capital, Felix Capital, and Daphni alongside existing backers.
Sereact develops hardware-agnostic Vision Language Action Models (VLAM) that enable robots to understand and adapt to environments in real-time without complex programming.
Founded in Stuttgart in 2021, Sereact's customers include Daimler Truck, Bol, MS Direct, and Active Ants.
The company takes a software-first approach, making robots function as intelligent adaptable agents rather than pre-programmed machines, with plans to expand into mobile robots and humanoids.
The company declined to disclose its valuation; the funding will support US expansion and development of AI for more complex tasks beyond logistics.

stories.headline: Germany's Sereact Raises $110M Series B for AI-Powered Industrial Robotics, Backed by BMW and PepsiCo

key_facts.fact: Stuttgart-based Sereact raised €93 million ($110 million) in a Series B round led by Headline
The company develops software that makes industrial robots smarter by enabling them to handle tasks they haven't been specifically trained on
BMW and PepsiCo are among the company's customers using its robotics AI platform
Bullhound Capital and Daphni are among the new investors participating in the funding round
The funding will be used to expand in the US and build an AI model for robots that predict consequences of their actions

stories.headline: Taiwan Court Sentences Ex-Tokyo Electron Engineer to 10 Years for Stealing TSMC Trade Secrets

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's Intellectual Property and Commercial Court sentenced former TSMC engineer Chen Li-ming (who later joined Tokyo Electron) to 10 years in prison for trade secret theft
Tokyo Electron Taiwan was fined US$4.76 million (NT$150 million) — the first case applying corporate liability under Taiwan's National Security Act
Four other individuals also received jail sentences in the case
The stolen data involved TSMC's proprietary semiconductor manufacturing processes

stories.headline: Tokyo Electron Cuts Ties With Veteran China Exec After Discovering Family Investments in Rival Chipmakers

key_facts.fact: Tokyo Electron severed ties with Jay Chen, who led the company's China operations, after discovering his family-linked investment structures were connected to Chinese chip start-ups developing competing tools
One of the start-ups linked to Chen transitioned from servicing Tokyo Electron equipment to developing competing chipmaking tools
Tokyo Electron became aware of the investment connections in late 2024, replaced Chen in early 2025, and later retained him temporarily as a special adviser before his contract expired
Tokyo Electron is a dominant supplier of semiconductor manufacturing tools, holding a leading global position in 'track systems' essential to the lithography process
